- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 7-day average is >10% above 30-day average, adjust forecast downward by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.6), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; increase forecast variance by ±1–2% for 3–5 day horizon.
- If sentiment is high and price is near 30-day moving average, model tends to overreact; apply smoothing filter to reduce lagged momentum bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows >+5% deviation from 14-day average, model is likely underestimating; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5%.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment momentum.
